memory_update.text: AAOI mapped as underfollowed hypothesis tied to downstream InP laser and AI optical-transceiver demand; survival requires proof of material InP-dependent 800G/1.6T revenue, capacity, and customer orders.

ASC mapped as underfollowed sulphuric-acid logistics hypothesis; survival requires vessel/cargo evidence showing actual corrosive chemical or sulphuric-acid trade exposure rather than generic product-tanker beta.

GHM mapped as underfollowed nuclear-qualified component supplier hypothesis; survival requires backlog or contract evidence showing nuclear, naval nuclear, or SMR work is material to revenue or margins.
TECK mapped as reference acid-byproduct anchor, not primary discovery target; useful for sulphuric-acid market context but diversified company exposure dilutes purity.

POET and ALMU mapped as speculative photonics-substitution or integration names; both require proof of qualified customers, production yields, and commercial revenue before moving beyond speculative_shadow.
ATKR mapped as second-order AI data-center electrical balance-of-plant candidate; survival requires evidence that data-center and utility demand can offset construction-cycle and pricing headwinds.

MG mapped as nuclear inspection/compliance services hypothesis; survival requires vertical-level disclosure proving nuclear or power-generation inspection work is material and higher-quality than legacy services.
GCUMF/GCU.V mapped as micro-cap speculative sulphuric-acid optionality via domestic SX-EW and planned acid plant; financing, permitting, sulphur feedstock, and dilution risks are primary chokepoints.
Need primary company-source verification for all ticker-level claims because current external context supports the theme bottlenecks more strongly than the individual company exposures.

Need market-pricing checks for each candidate: current market cap bucket, valuation, liquidity, analyst count, short interest, relative performance, and whether the chokepoint story is already discounted.

Need independent confirmation of external-context claims on InP prices, AXT backlog, Coherent and Lumentum capacity, sulphuric-acid trade flows, and Indonesian HPAL disruption before upgrading claim quality.

summary: Mapped ticker relationships for the candidate chunk across three New Hotspots sub-chains: InP/AI optical interconnects, sulphur/sulphuric-acid logistics, and nuclear/electrical infrastructure second-order beneficiaries. The strongest relationship evidence in this chunk is thematic rather than company-specific: external context supports InP export-control tightness, sulphuric-acid trade disruption, and a research mandate to look one or two layers beneath obvious leaders. Most ticker-level mappings remain hypotheses until filings, earnings calls, customer disclosures, fleet/cargo data, or project-level evidence confirms material revenue exposure.
